summary: The Don't Sell Kids' Data Act of 2025 prohibits data brokers from collecting, using, maintaining, selling, or transferring the personal data of children (under 13) and teens (ages 13 to 17) when they know the individual is a minor. Data brokers must delete any existing personal data of minors and set up a request mechanism for deletion. The bill provides for enforcement through the Federal Trade Commission, State Attorneys General, and private civil lawsuits brought by individuals.

affected_groups.effect: Must stop collecting, using, or transferring personal data of known minors, delete existing minor data, and comply with deletion requests within 10 days or face FTC enforcement, state lawsuits, and private civil actions.
Their personal data is protected from being collected, maintained, or sold by data brokers, and they or their parents can request deletion of their data.
Empowered to submit deletion requests for the personal data of children under 13 and act on behalf of teens.
Granted specific statutory powers and jurisdictions to investigate, penalize, and bring civil actions against data brokers who violate the Act.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

key_provisions: Data brokers are prohibited from collecting, using, maintaining, selling, licensing, renting, trading, transferring, releasing, disclosing, or providing access to the personal data of any individual they know is a child or teen.
Data brokers must delete any personal data they currently maintain on individuals they know are children or teens.

Data brokers must establish a clear, publicly available mechanism for teens, parents, legal guardians, or authorized agents to request the deletion of a minor's personal data, which the data broker must fulfill within 10 days.
Violations of this Act are treated as unfair or deceptive acts or practices under the Federal Trade Commission Act, allowing the Federal Trade Commission to enforce the law.
State attorneys general or other state officials may bring civil actions on behalf of state residents in federal district court to enforce compliance, obtain damages, or seek injunctions.
Individuals may bring civil actions against data brokers in federal district court, with a minimum statutory damage award of $1,000 per violation, which can be tripled for willful violations.
Rights and remedies under the private right of action cannot be waived by terms of service or pre-dispute arbitration agreements.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact financial appropriations or funding amounts allocated to the Federal Trade Commission or states to carry out enforcement.
The source text does not detail specific definitions of data categories beyond general personal data and unique persistent identifiers.

Data brokers must delete any existing personal data of minors and set up a request mechanism for deletion. summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a comprehensive restriction on data brokers regarding the personal data of minors, supported by multi-layered enforcement mechanisms including federal regulation, state government action, and individual lawsuits with mandatory attorney fees and non-waivable rights. The significance score reflects substantial change for the data broker industry and minor privacy rights.
